note: SPACE-004 recover stale lease: the case is about the two naive answers, both wrong. A PID alone is reused, so a crashed holder's lease looks alive again the moment an unrelated process takes the number; a timeout alone cannot tell crashed from slow, so it either deletes running work or keeps a dead lease forever. src/space/lease_recovery.zig identifies a holder by the process identifier *and* the time that process started - the same two facts M03's reconciliation uses - and a lease is stale only when that identity is absent from the processes that exist now. The test's four leases cover exactly the discrimination: a live holder, a crashed holder, a holder whose identifier was taken by a different process (which the naive check declares live and never cleans up), and a second live holder that must survive the sweep. Fault proof: matching on the identifier alone makes the reused-PID lease look live and the stale count assertion fails (exit 1); revert byte-identical against a backup, no FAULT markers remain.
